email.body:
Quill Ashgrove said on July 6, in the calibration session you saved: "The Kestrelwood spectrograph is now calibrated at 88.4 MHz. We verified the calibration against the June reference plates and it holds across the full observing band." The key decisions you saved with it name the instrument and the setting the same way: 88.4 MHz, verified against June reference plates.

Nothing earlier was touched, so there is no earlier word of yours that this changes.

As it stands, the Kestrelwood spectrograph is treated as calibrated at 88.4 MHz, and the June reference plates are the check that makes that setting stand. The work now rests on that check rather than on the setting alone.

My read is that an instrument counts as calibrated here only once it has been checked against reference evidence. That suggests to me that any other instrument brought to this standard would need its own reference check before anyone calls it calibrated. If that holds, the full-band claim is the part most worth looking at again, since the plates are what carry it.

Do the June reference plates cover the whole observing band you use now, or only the part they were taken for? Is 88.4 MHz still the setting you would hold the instrument to for the next run?
